paper.title: Pure Exploration in Infinitely-Armed Bandit Models with Fixed-Confidence

settings.name_in_paper: Infinite bandit model with reservoir distribution, (alpha,delta)/(alpha,epsilon,delta)-correct identification (lower bound)
unmapped: Goal: identify an arm whose mean is at least the (1-alpha)-quantile of the reservoir distribution minus epsilon (top-alpha fraction), w.p. >= 1-delta
Arms drawn from an arbitrary (possibly non-smooth) reservoir distribution with bounded support; learner can query new arms or resample old ones
Reward distributions form a one-parameter family parameterized by mean with continuous, monotone KL (Assumption 1); mu* < sup Theta (Assumption 2)
settings.definition_quote: An algorithm that returns an arm from $\GTargetEps$ with probability at least $1-\delta$ is said to be $(\alpha,\epsilon,\delta)$-correct. ... $\forall (\ArmMeasure, \ArmMean), \PrTrueModel{ \hat{s}_\tau \in \GTargetEps } \geq 1 - \delta.$

settings.name_in_paper: Infinite bandit model with reservoir, one-parameter exponential family rewards, (alpha,epsilon,delta)-correct identification
unmapped: Goal: identify an arm whose mean is within epsilon of the (1-alpha)-quantile of the reservoir distribution, w.p. >= 1-delta
Arms drawn from an arbitrary reservoir distribution with bounded support; no regularity assumption on the reservoir
Learner can sample new arms from the arm measure M
settings.definition_quote: In this section we assume that $P_{\ExpRewards}$ is a one-parameter exponential family ... We do not make any new assumptions on the reservoir distribution.

symbols.H_lb: 1/d(mu*, b_2) + sum_{i=2}^{m-1} 1/d(b_i, mu*), d the KL divergence between reward distributions, b_i the boundaries of the alpha-measure partition of the reservoir, m = ceil(1/alpha)

source.label: thm-lb
source.quote: Fix some $\alpha, \delta \in ]0,1[$. Any $(\alpha,\delta)$-correct algorithm needs an expected sample complexity $\ETrueModel{\tau}$ that is lower bounded as follows. \ETrueModel{\tau} \ge \left( \frac{1}{\ArmKL{\ArmMean^*}{b_2}} + \sum_{i=2}^{m-1} \frac{1}{\ArmKL{b_i}{\ArmMean^*}} \right) \log \frac{1}{2.4\delta}.

results.notes: epsilon = 0 version. Reduces to Kaufmann et al. (2016) finite BAI bound for uniform reservoir over K arms with alpha=1/K (Remark 2).

bound.regime: epsilon small enough that mu* + epsilon in Theta

symbols.q: number of partition subsets containing arms within epsilon of the top-alpha fraction

source.quote: Fix some $\alpha, \epsilon, \delta \in ]0,1[$, and let $q$ be the number of subsets containing arms within $\epsilon$ of the top $\alpha$ fraction. Any $(\alpha,\epsilon,\delta)$-correct algorithm needs an expected sample complexity $\ETrueModel{\tau}$ that is lower bounded as follows. ... \log \frac{1}{4\delta}.

results.notes: Stated as a remark with only a proof sketch (Mannor et al. strategy).

tuning: n = (1/alpha) log(2/delta) arms drawn from reservoir
beta(t,delta) = log(k_1 n t^gamma / delta), gamma > 1, k_1 > 2 sum_t t^{-gamma}

source.label: correctness
source.quote: With $\beta(t,\delta)$ defined in \eqref{explo-rate}, \texttt{$(\alpha,\epsilon)$-KL-LUCB} returns an arm from $\GTargetEps$ with probability at least $1-\delta$.

results.notes: (alpha,epsilon,delta)-correctness: probability of returning an arm outside the epsilon-relaxed top-alpha set is at most delta.

symbols.C_0: constant C_0(gamma) with C_0 >= gamma log(C_0) + 1 + gamma/e
symbols.H_bar: 2/epsilon^2 + sum_{i=2}^m 1/max(epsilon^2/2, d*(b_{i-1}, b_1)), d* the Chernoff information

conditions: holds with probability at least 1-7 delta
tuning: beta(t,delta) = log(k_1 n t^gamma / delta), gamma > 1

source.label: samplecomp
source.quote: Let $\alpha,\delta$ such that $0<\delta \leq \alpha \leq 1/3$. The \texttt{$(\alpha,\epsilon)$-KL-LUCB} algorithm with exploration rate $\beta(t,\delta)$ defined by \eqref{explo-rate} and a parameter $\epsilon>0$ is $(\alpha,\epsilon,\delta)$-correct and satisfies, with probability at least $1-7\delta$, \tau \le 12 C_0(\gamma) \overline{H}_{\alpha,\epsilon} \log^2 \frac{1}{\delta} + o\left( \log^2 \frac{1}{\delta} \right)

results.notes: Bound is leading term plus o(log^2(1/delta)); recorded with notation O keeping the explicit constant 12 C_0. Probability 1-7delta.
